**WHO WE ARE**


Volunteers of America Colorado is a nonprofit, faith\-based organization dedicated to helping those in\-need transform their lives. Through more than 50 distinct human service programs, Volunteers of America changes the lives of more than 140,000 vulnerable Coloradoans each year. VOA services include housing and emergency shelters, hunger and nutrition services, and many other community support programs. Our work touches the mind, body, heart and ultimately the spirit of those we serve. VOA integrates compassion with highly effective programs that build and strengthen communities.

**PROGRAM**


This position is for the Back Home SSVF (Supportive Services for Veteran Families) program which is a Rapid Rehousing program that utilizes a 90\-day model to find and stabilize housing for veterans experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness. Primarily focusing on housing case management, but also offering wrap\-around case management services assisting to connect veterans to Public Benefits, VA benefits, Health referrals, and Financial health referrals.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**


The Case Manager directs and facilitates the delivery of appropriate support services for participant households as indicated by relevant service modalities. Job duties include conducting needs\-based and program eligibility assessments, engaging in community outreach, providing case management services, and program\-wide service coordination. jobs.title: Young Adult Shelter Program Manager
jobs.description:
**Job Summary:**

Under the supervision of the Assistant Director of Shelter Services, the **Young Adult Shelter Program Manager** is responsible for the overall oversite and administration of the Young Adult Shelter program, which offers 24/7 services to youth ages 18\-24, and always ensures adequate staffing. This includes response to emergency situations, supervision of Life Skill Managers, full\-time volunteers, and relief staff. The Young Adult Shelter Program Manager is also responsible for the oversight of HMIS/Salesforce data quality, QMAP requirements, maintenance of physical space, as well as oversight of youth activities and working closely with the Assistant Director of Shelter Services to assist with shelter program development.

In addition, they will act as liaison between the Volunteer Coordinator and volunteers at the shelter, communicating needs and ensuring all volunteers feel welcome and have an understanding of the Young Adult Shelter.

This role will also be responsible for oversight and understanding of health department regulations, as well as training new staff in their positions. They will ensure that interactions, interventions and environments at Urban Peak are trauma informed and emphasize the physical and emotional safety of youth and staff.

**Who You Are:** 

* A master’s degree in social work, psychology, or child development AND a minimum of two (2\) years’ treatment\-oriented or case management experience; OR a bachelor’s degree in behavioral science, human services, or related fields AND three (3\) years’ experience working with children/youth; OR 5 years’ full\-time (FT) experience with homeless or runaway youth.
* Experience supervising staff and managing a residential and/or shelter program are preferred
* Confidence in timely and accurate data collection and the ability to maintain accurate and thorough client files (this position will utilize Salesforce)
* The ability to connect well, work effectively and communicate in a culturally responsive manner with a diverse youth population.
* Ability to handle multiple tasks and to assess and change priorities based upon agency and client needs, in an environment that sometimes includes interpersonal conflict and chaos
* Skilled in mediating and de\-escalating, particularly in sensitive situations.
* Able to make sound decisions, using available information while maintaining appropriate confidentiality.
* Able to function as a member of an interdisciplinary team and work with collaborating agencies.
* Must be team\-oriented and able to coordinate with various departments and staff.
* Lived experience reflective of the youth we serve encouraged but not required
* Must be computer proficient and possess experience of Microsoft Office Suite (e.g. Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel)
* Understanding of the provision of and commitment to trauma\-informed care and positive youth development
* Must be insurable as a driver on Urban Peak’s auto liability policy in order to conduct business on behalf of the agency or transport youth using an Urban Peak vehicle and/or an approved personal vehicle
* Must be QMAP\-certified or eligible for QMAP certification.
* Ability to use second language in written and verbal communication is desired but not a requirement (most common languages in the Denver Metro area).
* Must pass both federal and state background checks
* Must pass pre\-employment physical
* Must pass pre\-employment tuberculosis (TB) screening
* Ability to provide proof of education (HS Diploma OR Official Transcripts)

**What You Will Do:**

***Milieu Supervision***

* During coverage of floor shifts or on holiday and on\-call shifts, the Young Adult Shelter Program Manager focuses their attention on providing oversight of the shelter milieu area.
* Provides services for youth through a trauma informed approach, working to ensure the physical and emotional safety of the youth and their environment.
* Provides programming that supports the building of healthy relationships, as needed.
* Works alongside kitchen staff and volunteers to ensure meals are prepared in a safe, clean, and efficient manner.
* Works with youth to maintain cleanliness of their environment. Provides direction and support to youth on the completion of daily chores.
* Maintains a welcoming presence and support youth who enter the program through intakes, tours, and bed assignments.
* Provides crisis intervention and de\-escalation support, including verbal and physical altercations, and phone counseling, as needed.

**Documentation**

* Ensures accurate documentation of all services (including intakes, assessments, case notes, treatment plans, as well as individual and bulk services) in Salesforce.
* Ensures all client documentation is in accordance with programmatic data quality standards.
* Obtains Releases of Information for all communication with external supports on behalf of client.
* Documents significant events and client updates in the Communication Log.
* Maintains clear and effective communication with other staff regarding clients.
* Ensures client confidentiality through the safe and secure storage of client information.
* Completes thorough intakes in a manner that begins to establish comfort and trusting relationships.
* During intake, assesses the level of need and make recommendations regarding youth’s involvement in Urban Peak. Establishes plans with youth, ensures follow through, and makes appropriate referrals.

***Program Oversight***

* In conjunction with the Assistant Director of Shelter Services, maintains compliance with all the various grants and their programmatic requirements, shelter licensing requirements, responds to licensing inquiries as needed and participates in audits and licensing visits
* Oversees inventory and purchasing of shelter supplies.
* Plans and coordinates position\-specific training for new hires
* Plans and facilitates Shelter meetings in coordination with Assistant Director of Shelter Se

jobs.title: Social worker
jobs.description:
Are you a compassionate, dedicated professional looking to make a meaningful impact in the lives of patients and their families during their most vulnerable moments? Join the Bristol Hospice team as a **Hospice Social Worker**, where your work will play a critical role in providing comfort, support, and dignity to those nearing the end of life.  



Bristol Hospice is a nationwide industry leader committed to providing a family\-centered approach in the delivery of hospice services throughout our communities. We are dedicated to our mission that all patients and families entrusted to our care will be treated with the highest level of compassion, respect, and dignity. For more information about Bristol Hospice, visit bristolhospice.com or follow us on LinkedIn.  



**Our Culture**


Our culture is cultivated using the following values:

* **Integrity:** We are honest and professional.
* **Trust:** We count on each other.
* **Excellence:** We strive to always do our best and look for ways to improve and excel.
* **Accountability:** We accept responsibility for our actions, attitudes, and mistakes.
* **Mutual Respect:** We treat others the way we want to be treated.

**An Average Day:**  

*(Includes, but not limited to)*

* Assess the psychosocial status of patients and families/caregivers related to the patient's terminal illness and environment and communicates findings to the registered nurse and other members of the interdisciplinary group
* Provide an assessment in the patient's identified residence and assistance when this is not safe, and another plan is required
* Carry out social evaluations, including family dynamics, caregiver abilities, communication patterns, high risks for suicide, neglect or abuse and plan intervention based on evaluation findings
* Counsel patient and family/caregivers as needed in relationship to stress, and other identified coping difficulties; provide crisis intervention when necessary
* Assess for, and educate interdisciplinary group, on any special needs related to the culture of the patient and family, including communication, role of family, space, and any special traditions or taboos
* Maintain clinical records on all patients referred to social work
* Educate patients and families on, and assist in, preparation of advanced directives
* Provide information and referral services for organization patients and families/caregivers regarding practical and environmental needs
* Provide information to patients and families/caregivers and community agencies
* Serve as liaison between patients and families/caregivers and community agencies
* Maintain collaborative relationships with organization personnel to support patient care
* Maintain and develop contacts with public and private agencies as resources for patient and personnel
* Participate in the development of the individualized plan of care, involving the patient and family, and attend regularly scheduled interdisciplinary group meetings, assist the team in recognizing the effects of the psychosocial stresses on symptoms of the terminal illness
* Assist physician and other team members in understanding significant social and emotional factors related to health problems and death/dying issues
* Actively participate in quality assessment performance improvement teams and activities
* Assist family and patient in planning for funeral arrangements, financial, legal, and health care decision responsibilities
* Perform other duties as delegated by the Clinical Supervisor




**Requirements:**

* Must have a master’s degree in social work from an accredited university.
	+ If you hold an undergraduate B.A, Degree in Social Work, you are eligible to apply. Please know the hirable rate of pay will be based on degree type.
* Must have minimum of two (2\) years of documented supervised experience in health care, hospice experience preferred
* Must understand hospice philosophy, and issues of death/dying.
* Certified Hospice and Palliative Social Worker is desirable
* Must be flexible in work hours and have the ability to travel throughout the assigned Bristol Hospice service area
* Must demonstrate a willingness to maintain comprehensive working knowledge regarding information systems and applicable software programs




**We Got the Perks:**

* Tuition Reimbursement
* PTO and Paid Holidays
* Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, and more
* HSA \& 401(k) available
* Mileage Reimbursement for applicable positions
* Advanced training programs
* Passionate company culture committed to the highest standard of care in the hospice industry




***Join a Team that embraces the reverence of life!***




**EEOC Statement**




*Bristol Hospice is an equal\-opportunity employer. Our success depends upon our ability to create and maintain a diverse and supportive work environment where individuality is promoted. Bristol puts high priority on the worth of every person. We do not base our hiring decisions on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, age, disability, national or ethnic origin, military service status, citizenship, or other protected characteristics.*

### **Job Summary**

Advancement at CU Boulder encourages applications for an Annual Giving Program Coordinator! This role is responsible for helping secure new, recurring, and upgraded gifts under the $25,000 level in support of key performance indicators.  

Under the guidance of the Director of Annual Giving – Broad\-based Fundraising, this position supports the management of Annual Giving’s internal partnerships in fulfillment of broad\-based and multi\-channel fundraising campaigns. Through collaboration with school, college, and unit (SCU) Advancement teams, student groups, staff and faculty, this position will contribute to fundraising efforts that highlight the breadth of philanthropic opportunities at CU Boulder to a wide audience of alumni and other constituents. This is an entry\-level role meant to provide a pathway for a successful career in fundraising and relationship management.  

The Annual Giving team is a centralized team on the CU Boulder campus focused on creating and driving fundraising strategies supporting the acquisition and retention of entry\-level and mid\-level donors and moving donors through the major gift continuum. This team prioritizes the ethical collection and use of data to support operations built on best\-practices and champions a donor\-first philosophy towards the solicitation of donors giving gifts of less than $25,000 in support of the short and long\-term priorities of CU Boulder.  



CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.
### **Who We Are**

**CU Boulder Advancement** is committed to a culture of joy, motivated by collaboration, passionate about excellence and driven by impact. These four values define the culture and drive engagement and fundraising success.  

We are committed to fostering an environment where everyone matters and all can thrive. This dedication is rooted in our core values and our mission to drive impactful fundraising and engagement. Our team actively engages in learning, reflection, and the transformation of systems, policies, and practices that perpetuate oppressive ideologies—including racism, sexism, ableism, and heterosexism. We recognize our responsibility to lead by example in building a supportive and inclusive culture for both internal colleagues and external partners. We hold ourselves accountable through individual and divisional goals that continuously assess our progress, growth, and outcomes—ensuring alignment with our mission and values every step of the way.
### **What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be**

**Campus Support*** Manages the campus\-wide crowdfunding program, including identifying campaign opportunities and supporting those projects from inception to completion.
* Maintains working relationships with campus partners to facilitate affinity\-based fundraising opportunities.
* Supports multi\-channel annual giving campaigns that incorporate segmented content and/or audiences based on SCU affiliation.
* Supervises industry trends related to community fundraising and documents opportunities to implement standard processes at CU Boulder.
**Annual Giving*** Participates in the implementation of the agreed\-upon baseline on Annual Giving activities that are shared across CU, as described within the Annual Giving Memorandum of Understanding.
* Collaborates with colleagues across Advancement to achieve a cohesive approach to annual giving strategies and processes.
* Supports the pursuit of CU Boulder’s Annual Giving key performance indicators.
* Under the guidance of the Director of Annual Giving – Broad\-based Fundraising, reviews the effectiveness of Annual Giving programs and make suggestions for modifications and improvements.
**Data and Reporting*** Requests and organizes data to provide lists, segments, analysis, and reports to support campus projects.
* Ensures the on\-time and accurate delivery of data files and reports to internal and external partners as necessary.
* Supports the development and distribution of regular reports that enable Annual Giving and Advancement leadership to monitor, review, and celebrate fundraising activities.
* Assists CU Boulder Annual Giving with data\-driven decisions and analysis.

### **What You Should Know**

* This position may require local, regional, and out\-of\-state travel to engage with university constituents.
* This position is remote and will be required to travel to campus several times a year.
* This position will occasionally be required to work evenings/weekends.

### **What We Can Offer**

The salary range for this position is $57,000 \- $62,000 annually. Relocation assistance is available within Advancement guidelines.

At the University of Colorado Boulder, we are committed to supporting the holistic health and well\-being of our employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder offers an inspiring academic community and access to world\-class outdoor recreation. jobs.description:
**POSITION SUMMARY**


The **Spanish Interpreter** **PRN** provides accurate, confidential, and culturally competent spoken Spanish interpretation services for patients, families, and staff at Craig Hospital. This role supports effective communication across clinical and non\-clinical settings to ensure equitable access to care, patient safety, and compliance with legal and regulatory standards. The PRN Spanish Interpreter works under the direction of the Coordinator of Interpretive Services and collaborates with interdisciplinary teams to facilitate meaningful communication using in\-person and approved remote interpretive modalities. This position provides spoken Spanish interpretation only and does not include ASL or other signed language services.

  


**Location:** 3425 S Clarkson St, Englewood, CO 80113


**Shift:** PRN (Estimated 20 hours per week)


**Schedule:** Variable, based on patient care requirements. Fixed hours are not guaranteed


**Compensation:** $21\.59–$31\.09; plus an additional 18% PRN differential/hour


**Application Deadline:** Tuesday, August 25th, 2026\.

  


**WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR**


* Licensure/Certification/Registrations:
	+ Certified Healthcare Interpreter (CHI), National Board of Certification for Medical Interpreters (NBCMI), or equivalent; strongly preferred
	+ Demonstrated interpreter competency; required
* Education:
	+ High school diploma or equivalency, required.
	+ Formal interpreter training program completion is strongly preferred.
* Experience:
	+ Prior experience providing Spanish interpretation in a healthcare setting; preferred
	+ Familiarity with hospital or rehabilitation environments a plus
* Skills \& Abilities:
	+ Native or near\-native fluency in spoken Spanish and English.
	+ Ability to accurately interpret medical terminology and complex clinical discussions.
	+ Strong interpersonal skills, professional judgment, cultural humility, and attention to detail.
	+ Ability to maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries at all times.
	+ Computer proficiency required; Epic (EMR) experience preferred.
**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**


**Interpretation Services**


* Provide accurate, complete, and impartial Spanish interpretation during clinical encounters including therapies, physician visits, admissions, discharges, care conferences, education sessions, and non\-clinical interactions.


* Interpret according to national standards of practice and ethical guidelines for healthcare interpreters.


* Utilize approved in\-person or remote interpretive technology as assigned.


Coordination \& Communication


* Accept assignments and scheduling direction from the Coordinator of Interpretive Services.


* Communicate availability, schedule changes, and concerns promptly and professionally.


* Collaborate respectfully with physicians, therapists, nursing staff, and interdisciplinary team members to support patient\-centered communication.


**Compliance \& Quality Assurance**


* Maintain strict adherence to HIPAA, patient confidentiality, and hospital policies.


* Uphold professional boundaries and neutrality; refrain from advocacy, counseling, or personal opinions during interpretation.


* Participate in quality assurance activities, peer feedback, and performance improvement initiatives as requested.


**Documentation \& Administrative Support**


* Complete required documentation in Epic (EMR) according to department standards.


* Accurately track and submit hours worked and encounter information.


* Report ethical concerns, safety risks, or communication barriers to the Coordinator of Interpretive Services promptly.


* This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties. The employee may perform other related duties as assigned.

We have *Tuition Assistance.* Unexpected emergency? We have *Employee Assistance Programs*. For Craig, we believe in offering best in class benefits and, we prioritize benefits to support you.

  


**JOIN CRAIG HOSPITAL**


Nationally recognized for our excellence in spinal cord and brain injury rehabilitation, Craig Hospital is more than a care facility—it’s a tight\-knit community of healthcare professionals committed to transforming lives. Our nurses play a critical role in that transformation, combining technical skill with human compassion in a collaborative, interdisciplinary setting.

* **Unmatched Clinical Growth:** Master advanced neurological and respiratory interventions.

jobs.title: Part Time Certified Community Health Worker
jobs.description:
At Caregenix, we are committed to delivering exceptional, value\-based care. Our team lives by the iCARE values—Integrity, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence—in everything we do. If you are passionate about improving patient outcomes and providing compassionate care in a remote setting, we want to hear from you.

**Position Summary:**

The Community Health Worker (CHW) supports patients in addressing non\-medical, "upstream" factors \- such as housing, food access, transportation, and social support \- that affect their ability to manage their health condition. The CHW works as auxiliary personnel under the general supervision of a billing practitioner (physician, NP, PA, or certified nurse midwife) to deliver Medicare\-reimbursable Community Health Integration (CHI) services.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Conduct person\-centered assessments to identify social and environmental barriers to care
* Coordinate services with healthcare providers, facilities, and home\- and community\-based resources
* Provide health education and support patient self\-advocacy skill\-building
* Facilitate patient behavioral change to support diagnosis and treatment goals
* Facilitate and provide social and emotional support to the patient
* Leverage relevant lived experience, as applicable, to support, mentor, or inspire patient goal attainment
* Connect patients to community\-based resources (food, housing, transportation, financial assistance, etc.)
* Maintain regular contact with assigned patients following the practitioner's initiating visit
* Accurately document time spent, services provided, and patient consent in the medical record

**Qualifications:**

* State licensure/certification, if required by the practicing state

jobs.description:
**Job Overview**

The Case Coordinator serves as Nova Nest NPO's designated operational lead for scholarship coordination, supportive housing communications, and privacy\-sensitive recipient information. The position manages the intake, verification, ongoing qualification, documentation, and provider communication necessary to administer housing and related supportive\-service scholarships in a manner that protects client privacy and limits access to protected health information, substance use disorder information, and other confidential recipient information.

This is a non\-clinical coordination role. The Case Coordinator does not diagnose, treat, counsel, provide medical advice, or provide the clinical judgment or responsibilities of any licensed provider, treatment program, sober living provider, case manager, or emergency service.

**Responsibilities**

**1\. Scholarship Intake, Review, and Eligibility Monitoring**

* Receive and organize scholarship inquiries, applications, referrals, provider communications, and requests for housing, food/basic needs, transportation, medication copay, or other approved supportive assistance.

**2\. Provider, Sober Living Home, and Case Manager Communications**

* Serve as the primary Nova Nest contact for sober living home providers, recovery residence partners, treatment\-related partners, referring case managers, and care coordination contacts for scholarship matters.
* Coordinate with providers regarding start dates, discharge dates, residency status, weekly rates, prorated charges, census updates, attendance or participation confirmations, billing questions, and scholarship\-related concerns.
* Maintain professional relationships with case managers and referring partners, including timely follow\-up, clear documentation, and appropriate boundaries regarding clinical matters.
* Request, receive, and verify only the recipient information necessary to determine scholarship eligibility, confirm continued qualification, and support approved payments.
* Escalate safety, discharge, noncompliance, or funding issues to the Board\-designated lead, or other authorized party without disclosing unnecessary clinical or substance use disorder details.

**3\. Confidential Records, HIPAA, and 42 CFR Part 2 Safeguards**

* Maintain confidential scholarship files, communications, provider invoices, eligibility documentation, releases of information, consent records, case manager updates, and recipient\-status information in a restricted\-access location approved by Nova Nest.
* Serve as Nova Nest's first\-line privacy checkpoint for scholarship\-related protected health information, substance use disorder information, and other client\-identifying information received from treatment providers, sober living providers, case managers, or other partners.
* Apply the minimum necessary standard to requests, uses, disclosures, reports, payment packets, emails, text messages, meeting summaries, and Board or finance updates.
* Confirm that any required release of information, authorization, consent, business associate agreement, qualified service organization agreement, provider agreement, or other privacy document is in place before requesting, receiving, using, or disclosing confidential recipient information, as applicable.
* Ensure that 42 CFR Part 2 information, is not redisclosed except as permitted by written consent, applicable law, or an appropriate court order, and that required notices or consent scope information accompany Part 2 disclosures when required.
* Avoid placing client names, diagnoses, treatment status, substance use disorder information, or other sensitive details in payment memos, public\-facing documents, general meeting minutes, fundraising materials, grant narratives, or Board reports.
* Maintain a secure recipient\-code crosswalk that links client names to internal scholarship IDs; restrict the crosswalk to the Case Coordinator and any other specifically authorized privacy\-role personnel.
* Report suspected privacy incidents, misdirected communications, unauthorized disclosures, lost devices, compromised accounts, or other confidentiality concerns promptly according to Nova Nest policy.

**4\. Invoice Review and Payment Packet Preparation**

* Receive provider invoices or billing support when they contain client\-identifying information or other confidential recipient details.
* Review invoices against approved scholarship terms, verified dates of service, residency status, authorized rates, prorations, funding caps, and any prior payments.
* Resolve invoice discrepancies with providers before payment authorization is sent to finance.
* Prepare a payment packet for the Treasurer or Controller using the minimum necessary information, typically including provider/payee, invoice number, service category, scholarship ID or recipient code, approved dates or billing period, approved amount, due date, funding source if applicable, and Case Coordinator approval.
* Retain confidential backup documentation in the restricted scholarship file rather than attaching PHI\-heavy records to accounting ledgers or general finance folders.

**5\. Documentation, Reporting, and Audit Trail**

* Maintain a current scholarship tracker showing active, pending, closed, denied, and waitlisted scholarships, using coded or de\-identified information for reports outside the privacy role.
* Document weekly or otherwise scheduled updates for recipient status, provider invoices, payments pending, funding needs, eligibility concerns, discharge notices, and scholarship term expirations.
* Provide de\-identified and aggregated reporting to leadership and the Board, such as number of active scholarships, provider totals, approved amounts, outstanding payment packets, utilization trends, and funding needs.
* Support grant, audit, and compliance requests by preparing de\-identified program data and coordinating any necessary privacy review before client\-level information is shar

**Location:** United States / Europe \| Remote  
**Work Hours:** US \& EU Overlap  
**Role:** Program Coordinator  
**Global Collaboration:** US \| India \| EU

**About the Role**

We are looking for a highly organized and proactive **Program Coordinator** to support a complex global engagement involving teams across the **US, India, and Europe**.

Your job is to make multiple time zones feel like **one coordinated program**—keeping meetings organized, actions moving, communications clear, and operational details under control.

This is a hands\-on coordination role for someone who takes ownership, follows through relentlessly, and is comfortable working across multiple teams, vendors, and stakeholders.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Coordinate meetings and schedules across **US, India, and European time zones**.
* Prepare agendas, capture **meeting minutes**, and maintain action\-item trackers.
* Follow up with stakeholders to ensure actions are completed on time.
* Provide day\-to\-day **program communications and coordination support**.
* Support **training logistics**, including scheduling, participant coordination, materials, and follow\-ups.
* Support **change\-management activities and communications**.
* Coordinate with vendors and provide operational support for vendor\-related activities.
* Maintain organized program documentation and communication records.
* Track deadlines, dependencies, and outstanding actions across workstreams.
* Help ensure information flows efficiently between geographically distributed teams.
* Provide administrative and operational support to program leadership as required.

**Must\-Have Qualifications**

* **2–4 years of experience** coordinating complex programs, projects, or executive operations.
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders simultaneously.
* **Exceptional follow\-through**—you don't just track actions; you make sure they get closed.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Excellent organization and attention to detail.
* Comfortable coordinating across **multiple time zones and regions**.
* Ability to work independently in a fast\-moving, multi\-workstream environment.

**Strong Plus:**

* **Portuguese language proficiency**
* Previous experience supporting **multi\-region or global programs**
* Experience coordinating teams across the **US, India, and Europe**
* Experience with **training coordination or change\-management activities**
* Vendor coordination experience

**What We’re Looking For**

We’re looking for someone who is **organized, dependable, proactive, and relentless about follow\-through**.

If an action item is assigned to you, it shouldn't disappear into a spreadsheet—it should get **tracked, followed up, and closed**.

If you enjoy bringing order to complex programs and keeping globally distributed teams aligned, we'd like to hear from you.

* Life insurance

new_jobs.title: Social worker
new_jobs.description:
Are you a compassionate, dedicated professional looking to make a meaningful impact in the lives of patients and their families during their most vulnerable moments? Join the Bristol Hospice team as a **Hospice Social Worker**, where your work will play a critical role in providing comfort, support, and dignity to those nearing the end of life.  



Bristol Hospice is a nationwide industry leader committed to providing a family\-centered approach in the delivery of hospice services throughout our communities. We are dedicated to our mission that all patients and families entrusted to our care will be treated with the highest level of compassion, respect, and dignity. For more information about Bristol Hospice, visit bristolhospice.com or follow us on LinkedIn.  



**Our Culture**


Our culture is cultivated using the following values:

* **Integrity:** We are honest and professional.
* **Trust:** We count on each other.
* **Excellence:** We strive to always do our best and look for ways to improve and excel.
* **Accountability:** We accept responsibility for our actions, attitudes, and mistakes.
* **Mutual Respect:** We treat others the way we want to be treated.

**An Average Day:**  

*(Includes, but not limited to)*

* Assess the psychosocial status of patients and families/caregivers related to the patient's terminal illness and environment and communicates findings to the registered nurse and other members of the interdisciplinary group
* Provide an assessment in the patient's identified residence and assistance when this is not safe, and another plan is required
* Carry out social evaluations, including family dynamics, caregiver abilities, communication patterns, high risks for suicide, neglect or abuse and plan intervention based on evaluation findings
* Counsel patient and family/caregivers as needed in relationship to stress, and other identified coping difficulties; provide crisis intervention when necessary
* Assess for, and educate interdisciplinary group, on any special needs related to the culture of the patient and family, including communication, role of family, space, and any special traditions or taboos
* Maintain clinical records on all patients referred to social work
* Educate patients and families on, and assist in, preparation of advanced directives
* Provide information and referral services for organization patients and families/caregivers regarding practical and environmental needs
* Provide information to patients and families/caregivers and community agencies
* Serve as liaison between patients and families/caregivers and community agencies
* Maintain collaborative relationships with organization personnel to support patient care
* Maintain and develop contacts with public and private agencies as resources for patient and personnel
* Participate in the development of the individualized plan of care, involving the patient and family, and attend regularly scheduled interdisciplinary group meetings, assist the team in recognizing the effects of the psychosocial stresses on symptoms of the terminal illness
* Assist physician and other team members in understanding significant social and emotional factors related to health problems and death/dying issues
* Actively participate in quality assessment performance improvement teams and activities
* Assist family and patient in planning for funeral arrangements, financial, legal, and health care decision responsibilities
* Perform other duties as delegated by the Clinical Supervisor




**Requirements:**

* Must have a master’s degree in social work from an accredited university.
	+ If you hold an undergraduate B.A, Degree in Social Work, you are eligible to apply. Please know the hirable rate of pay will be based on degree type.
* Must have minimum of two (2\) years of documented supervised experience in health care, hospice experience preferred
* Must understand hospice philosophy, and issues of death/dying.
* Certified Hospice and Palliative Social Worker is desirable
* Must be flexible in work hours and have the ability to travel throughout the assigned Bristol Hospice service area
* Must demonstrate a willingness to maintain comprehensive working knowledge regarding information systems and applicable software programs




**We Got the Perks:**

* Tuition Reimbursement
* PTO and Paid Holidays
* Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, and more
* HSA \& 401(k) available
* Mileage Reimbursement for applicable positions
* Advanced training programs
* Passionate company culture committed to the highest standard of care in the hospice industry




***Join a Team that embraces the reverence of life!***

*Bristol Hospice is an equal\-opportunity employer. Our success depends upon our ability to create and maintain a diverse and supportive work environment where individuality is promoted. Bristol puts high priority on the worth of every person. We do not base our hiring decisions on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, age, disability, national or ethnic origin, military service status, citizenship, or other protected characteristics.*

new_jobs.description:
**Job Overview**

The Case Coordinator serves as Nova Nest NPO's designated operational lead for scholarship coordination, supportive housing communications, and privacy\-sensitive recipient information. The position manages the intake, verification, ongoing qualification, documentation, and provider communication necessary to administer housing and related supportive\-service scholarships in a manner that protects client privacy and limits access to protected health information, substance use disorder information, and other confidential recipient information.

This is a non\-clinical coordination role. The Case Coordinator does not diagnose, treat, counsel, provide medical advice, or provide the clinical judgment or responsibilities of any licensed provider, treatment program, sober living provider, case manager, or emergency service.

**Responsibilities**

**1\. Scholarship Intake, Review, and Eligibility Monitoring**

* Receive and organize scholarship inquiries, applications, referrals, provider communications, and requests for housing, food/basic needs, transportation, medication copay, or other approved supportive assistance.

**2\. Provider, Sober Living Home, and Case Manager Communications**

* Serve as the primary Nova Nest contact for sober living home providers, recovery residence partners, treatment\-related partners, referring case managers, and care coordination contacts for scholarship matters.
* Coordinate with providers regarding start dates, discharge dates, residency status, weekly rates, prorated charges, census updates, attendance or participation confirmations, billing questions, and scholarship\-related concerns.
* Maintain professional relationships with case managers and referring partners, including timely follow\-up, clear documentation, and appropriate boundaries regarding clinical matters.
* Request, receive, and verify only the recipient information necessary to determine scholarship eligibility, confirm continued qualification, and support approved payments.
* Escalate safety, discharge, noncompliance, or funding issues to the Board\-designated lead, or other authorized party without disclosing unnecessary clinical or substance use disorder details.

**3\. Confidential Records, HIPAA, and 42 CFR Part 2 Safeguards**

* Maintain confidential scholarship files, communications, provider invoices, eligibility documentation, releases of information, consent records, case manager updates, and recipient\-status information in a restricted\-access location approved by Nova Nest.
* Serve as Nova Nest's first\-line privacy checkpoint for scholarship\-related protected health information, substance use disorder information, and other client\-identifying information received from treatment providers, sober living providers, case managers, or other partners.
* Apply the minimum necessary standard to requests, uses, disclosures, reports, payment packets, emails, text messages, meeting summaries, and Board or finance updates.
* Confirm that any required release of information, authorization, consent, business associate agreement, qualified service organization agreement, provider agreement, or other privacy document is in place before requesting, receiving, using, or disclosing confidential recipient information, as applicable.
* Ensure that 42 CFR Part 2 information, is not redisclosed except as permitted by written consent, applicable law, or an appropriate court order, and that required notices or consent scope information accompany Part 2 disclosures when required.
* Avoid placing client names, diagnoses, treatment status, substance use disorder information, or other sensitive details in payment memos, public\-facing documents, general meeting minutes, fundraising materials, grant narratives, or Board reports.
* Maintain a secure recipient\-code crosswalk that links client names to internal scholarship IDs; restrict the crosswalk to the Case Coordinator and any other specifically authorized privacy\-role personnel.
* Report suspected privacy incidents, misdirected communications, unauthorized disclosures, lost devices, compromised accounts, or other confidentiality concerns promptly according to Nova Nest policy.

**4\. Invoice Review and Payment Packet Preparation**

* Receive provider invoices or billing support when they contain client\-identifying information or other confidential recipient details.
* Review invoices against approved scholarship terms, verified dates of service, residency status, authorized rates, prorations, funding caps, and any prior payments.
* Resolve invoice discrepancies with providers before payment authorization is sent to finance.
* Prepare a payment packet for the Treasurer or Controller using the minimum necessary information, typically including provider/payee, invoice number, service category, scholarship ID or recipient code, approved dates or billing period, approved amount, due date, funding source if applicable, and Case Coordinator approval.
* Retain confidential backup documentation in the restricted scholarship file rather than attaching PHI\-heavy records to accounting ledgers or general finance folders.

**5\. Documentation, Reporting, and Audit Trail**

* Maintain a current scholarship tracker showing active, pending, closed, denied, and waitlisted scholarships, using coded or de\-identified information for reports outside the privacy role.
* Document weekly or otherwise scheduled updates for recipient status, provider invoices, payments pending, funding needs, eligibility concerns, discharge notices, and scholarship term expirations.
* Provide de\-identified and aggregated reporting to leadership and the Board, such as number of active scholarships, provider totals, approved amounts, outstanding payment packets, utilization trends, and funding needs.

The Case Manager I position will have a full understanding of the Enhanced Case Management (ECM) suite of strategies and supports the Enhanced Care Advocate and ECM team. **ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Review clinicals, claims and baseline case information for health scenarios such as Behavioral, Wellness, and Specialty Prescription, Maternity etc.

* Work closely with the Clinical Case Management team and other Case Managers to obtain clinical information needed to support the care plan. This includes case presentation when needed to discuss collaboratively to identify and troubleshoot escalated issues within case work.
